title: Priority-queue eviction hysteresis and SLO regression postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2025-02-17 a coordinated surge in traffic to US-West created persistent priority-queue evictions in the control plane which, combined with overly permissive circuit hysteresis thresholds in EU regions, caused cascading failovers and a temporary SLO miss for 95th/99th tail latency across chat and generation routes. This document captures the timeline, root causes, and a prioritized action plan to avoid recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-17T09:10Z - Alert: US-West p95 CPU climb and per-route queue depth increase. Initial paging to on-call infra team.
2025-02-17T09:14Z - Automated circuit breaker policy triggered in US-West but hysteresis settings delayed failback; secondary routing sent to EU clusters.
2025-02-17T09:22Z - EU regions began receiving cross-region fanout; observed increased latency and growth in KV cache thrash in EU-1 nodes.

2025-02-17T09:35Z - Control plane priority eviction policy (for reserved burst capacity) started evicting medium-priority requests in US-West; critical low-priority tokens were preserved incorrectly due to a weight inversion bug.
2025-02-17T09:50Z - Multiple canary circuits in EU flipped to heavy-backoff; downstream model-serving pools saw degraded throughput and token-level errors increased.
2025-02-17T10:10Z - SLO monitors tripped for chat-generation p95 and p99 across regions. Post-incident mitigation actions began (throttle adjustments, targeted circuit resets).
2025-02-17T11:00Z - Traffic quarantined to US-West priority lanes with manual override; cache warmup scripts executed on EU hot shards.
2025-02-17T12:20Z - System returned to steady-state. Incident declared mitigated at 2025-02-17T12:35Z. Postmortem investigation started.
2025-02-18T14:00Z - Engineering rotation review and preliminary findings recorded. This ticket created to track follow-ups.
impact: SLOs affected: chat/generation p95 and p99 latency exceeded target for ~1h 45m across cross-region failovers.
Customer symptoms: transient increased latencies, some streaming timeouts, a handful of token-generation errors. No data loss.
Scope: Approximately 9% of global requests experienced >2x latency temporarily; enterprise dedicated tenants in EU observed higher tail latency due to cross-region KV cache cold starts.
root_causes: 1) Priority-queue eviction logic regressed: a weight inversion introduced in PR #5822 caused medium-priority requests to be deprioritized relative to low-priority during high burst conditions.
2) Circuit breaker hysteresis thresholds were tuned for aggressive stability (long hold times) which prevented timely failback after transient relief, amplifying cross-region routing and load.
3) Cross-region routing did not account for KV cache cold-start costs; failed failover placements lacked a warmup path so downstream model shards experienced thrash.
4) Control-plane dashboards lacked a combined view of priority-queue evictions + circuit hysteresis state, delaying diagnosis by ~18 minutes.
5) Load-shedding policy had insufficient per-tenant caps for reserved capacity, permitting burst noise to evict non-burst workloads.
mitigation_taken: Manual throttles applied to US-West burst tokens and a manual override to restore medium-priority weights (09:55-10:05).
Targeted circuit resets in EU region to accelerate failback (10:00-10:15).
Deployed cache prewarm job to hot shards and disabled cross-region routing for low-priority routes for 30 minutes to stabilize KV hit rates.
Rolled back PR #5822 within 40 minutes of detection; medium-priority weight restored.
Communicated with affected customers via status.redwood.ai and posted a summary in #incident-updates.
lessons_learned: Circuit hysteresis needs to be tier-aware: long hold times are valuable for noisy sources, but they should be bounded per-tenant and per-route to avoid cross-region amplification.
Priority-queue logic must be covered by mutation- and behavior-level unit tests. Current unit tests did not capture weight inversion nor integration with quota rules.
Prewarm/gradual-fanout strategy for KV cache should be part of any cross-region redirect to avoid cold-start penalties on hot shards.
Dashboarding: combine eviction metrics and circuit state in one operational pane to reduce mean time to detect and triage.

notes: Root cause was a conjunction of small failures rather than a single catastrophic bug. Fixing the weight inversion removed immediate pain but systemic hardening is required.
Team rotation and on-call handover notes indicate correlation confusion between 'queue depth' and 'eviction rate' metrics; alert definitions will be updated.
We observed that dedicated tenants with pinned models had disproportionate cold-start costs when placed in a non-warm region; prioritization logic should favor warm placement when possible.
